promptText: Research Suite (科研套件) is the project container for multi-step research here. Use it whenever the task will outlive one answer: literature reviews, replications, data analyses, evaluations, due diligence, or anything the user calls a 研究/项目/综述/复现/尽调/评测. A campaign has nine gates: scoping → survey → hypothesis → design → execute → analyze → write → review → release. Start with rsx_template action:"apply" (11 task presets + replication/ablation/adversarial-review protocols) or rsx_campaign action:"create". Record the question, scope and success criteria, then run rsx_gate action:"check" before advancing. Before each iteration call rsx_campaign action:"loop": it checks integrity, budget, the gate and the autonomy cycle budget, then returns continue, pause, stop or ready. It records a pause (LP-xxxx plus a loop.paused event) when the primary action needs input, a human checkpoint or an unmapped gate recipe; it never runs or approves the action. Stop there and resume only after the input is supplied, with action:"loop" resume:true; an unchanged blocker is rejected, a cleared one records loop.resumed. Use action:"next" for the read-only plan without the loop control. For sector work select a domain profile with rsx_domain action:"set": finance, ai, medicine or industrial. A profile turns protocol fields into blocking checks at their stages (point-in-time/OOS dates, TRIPOD+AI, PRISMA counts, MSA/DOE, review roles, monitoring); conditional fields switch off when the design/risk tier makes them inapplicable. It is an alignment checklist, not a certification claim. Use rsx_domain action:"check" to see the exact missing fields for the current stage. Log as you work, not at the end: rsx_search for live OpenAlex/Crossref metadata discovery (read-only, DOI-deduplicated, bounded; a provider failure is a warning, never a citation), rsx_source for what you actually read (action:"import" ingests Zotero/Scholar BibTeX), rsx_claim for what you assert, rsx_evidence to link claim↔source/run, rsx_run for a real command + seed + metrics, rsx_number for every number with trace run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#metric or source:S-0001, rsx_extract to build the source × dimension matrix, rsx_artifact for datasets/code/environments, rsx_figure for figure+code+data provenance. Register only candidates you inspected; record the retrieval protocol with rsx_campaign action:"searchLog". For schema-3+ campaigns also log the database, query, dates and hits/screened/included of every search and rsx_claim action:"sensitivity" (changed specification, result, direction, optional trace); lock the pre-registration before the first run. Numbers in the manuscript are written as {{N-0001}} and citations as [[src:S-0001]]; the write gate rejects orphan digits and unknown refs. For schema-4 campaigns build the research programme with rsx_program (action:"plan"/"perspective"/"autonomy"/"cycle"/"match"/"quality"/"contradiction"): at least two covered plan questions, two sourced perspectives, an explicit maxCycles/stopCriteria/escalation/humanCheckpoints policy, one act→observe→decide cycle, one pairwise claim match, a six-dimension rubric with overall≥0.7, and no open contradictions. The review gate blocks until the programme is complete; the Elo ranking and rubric are bookkeeping, not proof. Before the review gate, run rsx_review action:"audit": it checks citations resolve, quotes occur in the captured text, numbers match the run that produced them, figures carry code+data, the pre-registration still describes the analysis, and domain fields/roles are present. Findings are blocking/major/minor/info; only blocking stops the gate, and any later edit makes the audit stale. For a domain campaign add one rsx_gate action:"review" per domain role (affiliation, conflict, independent, qualification), then audit after those reviews. Never invent a ledger entry: run the command first, then record what actually happened. If a gate blocks, read detail.blocking and fix the checks instead of working around them. Before delivery call rsx_write action:"declaration" (AI + watermark + human reviewer), record rsx_campaign action:"monitor" (plan, owner, cadence, metrics, observations), run rsx_campaign action:"evaluate" for the 13-dimension loop score, then action:"export", and give the user the REPORT.md path plus PROGRAM.md / LOOP.md / DOMAIN.md / references.bib / AUDIT.md / provenance.json. The sidebar panel shows the same state; the user can create campaigns, inspect the ledger, browse templates, edit domain/monitoring state, run the loop evaluation and read the report there. Continue an existing campaign by reading rsx_campaign action:"status" rather than starting over.

schemas.name: rsx_campaign
schemas.description: Research campaign control room: create/list/get/update a campaign, record the world model, the disconfirming search, the pre-registration and budget spend, and inspect integrity. A campaign moves through scoping → survey → hypothesis → design → execute → analyze → write → review → release. Use this first, then the entity tools (source/claim/evidence/run/number/extract/artifact/figure/review), then rsx_gate to advance. action:"search" records a disconfirming search; action:"searchLog" records any database/snowball/grey search with its query, date window and hit/screened/included counts. The searches are executed externally; this tool only keeps the protocol auditable. action:"status" returns the current stage, the gate state and the hash-chain integrity; action:"world" records entities/facts/questions/failures/coverage/novelty/safety used by the gates; action:"monitor" records the post-release monitoring plan that closes the loop; action:"evaluate" scores 13 research-loop dimensions, persists a baseline and returns the gaps. action:"portfolio" is a read-only cross-campaign view (score, level, audit freshness, alert count, integrity, attention reasons); action:"graph" returns the claim/source/run/number edge list for one campaign. action:"archive" shelves any campaign that is not busy, even before release, and action:"unarchive" restores it with the full ledger; archive is reversible, export remains gated by release. action:"next" is a deterministic planner: it returns one primary next tool call plus alternatives, ordered by the current gate and the programme gaps. It never writes or auto-approves; human checkpoints are marked and integrity/budget/prereg-timing failures stop the plan. action:"loop" is the host-loop checkpoint to call before each iteration: it verifies integrity/budget/gate/cycle budget and returns continue, pause, stop or ready. A pause is recorded as an LP-xxxx row and a loop.paused event when the primary action needs input, a human or an unmapped gate recipe; it never runs the action or approves. After the input is supplied call action:"loop" resume:true; an unchanged blocker is rejected, a cleared one records loop.resumed. 1.0 stewardship: action:"stewardship" sets the FAIR/CRediT fields (license, data/code availability, competing interests, ethics, funding, keywords, contributors); schema-5 release blocks until they are complete. action:"migrate" is the explicit schema upgrade: it verifies, writes a state+ledger backup, records campaign.migrated and can dry-run first. action:"doctor" is a read-only health scan (chain, state, artifacts, index, locks, audits, migrations); action:"reindex" rebuilds only index.json from the campaign directories.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

question.description: The research question (create/update). At least 12 characters for the scoping gate.

scope.description: Boundaries: what is in and out of scope.

numbersAllowlist.description: Comma/space separated constants allowed in the manuscript without a ledger trace (update action).

tier.description: Effort tier; S=60k tokens, M=400k, L=2M, XL=12M.

stewardship.description: FAIR/CRediT fields: {license, licenseUrl, dataAvailability, codeAvailability, funding:[], competingInterests, ethics, keywords:[], contributors:[{name, roles:[CRediT role], orcid, affiliation}]}. Also accepted at create and migrate.

dryRun.description: For migrate: report the missing stewardship fields and target schema without writing a backup or changing state.

domain.description: Optional domain profile id at create: finance, ai, medicine, industrial, or general.

values.description: Optional domain field values at create, keyed by field id (see rsx_domain action:"list").

monitoring.description: For monitor: {plan, owner, cadence, signals:[...], status:"planned"|"active"|"paused"|"closed"|"alert", reviewedAt, notes, metrics:[{name,target,tolerance,direction,min,max,unit}], observations:[{metric,value,at,note}]}.

observations.description: Monitoring observations: {metric,value,at,note}; values are evaluated against the registered metric (monitor action).

reopen.description: For monitor: move a released campaign back to analyze when an alert requires rework.

reason.description: Why the loop is reopened (monitor) or why a pause is resumed (loop).

resume.description: For loop: resume after the missing input or human checkpoint was supplied; an unchanged blocker is rejected.

kind.description: World bucket for world set/get: entity, fact, question, failure, coverage, novelty, safety.

value.description: World value; for novelty a plain string records {checked:true, nearest}. For safety use dual_use:"pass".

query.description: Query used for the disconfirming search (or searchLog).

disconfirming.description: Set true to record that a disconfirming search was run.

database.description: Database/source searched, e.g. PubMed, CNKI, Google Scholar (searchLog).

hits.description: Raw hits returned by the query (searchLog).

spec.description: Pre-registration: {hypothesisId, metric, n, analysisPlan, stoppingRule, seed, controls:["negative"], envLock, alpha, power, effectSize, test}. A locked protocol must be amended with amend:true + reason.

amend.description: For prereg: confirm a protocol amendment after the hash was locked.

tokens.description: Tokens to charge to the stage budget.

seconds.description: Seconds to charge to the stage budget.

schemas.name: rsx_search
schemas.description: Live literature metadata search on the host: queries OpenAlex and Crossref public APIs and returns normalized candidates with title, year, authors, DOI, URL, venue, abstract and citation count. This is read-only: it does not write the ledger, download full text or trust provider text as instructions. Register selected items with rsx_source; record the protocol with rsx_campaign action:"searchLog". provider:"both" is the default; a failed provider is reported in warnings, and only all-providers-failed is an error. Results are bounded, DOI-deduplicated and never fabricated.

query.description: Bibliographic query, e.g. "multi-agent research systems". Required; maximum 500 characters.

schemas.name: rsx_template
schemas.description: Research templates: 11 task presets (literature review, clinical trials, ML pipeline, health trends, paper slides, interview synthesis, OSS evaluation, quant backtest, academic site, due diligence, industrial DOE) plus 3 method protocols (replication, ablation, adversarial review). Templates tagged with a domain start the campaign with finance/ai/medicine/industrial checks already active. action:"apply" creates a campaign pre-filled from the template and returns a ready-to-paste prompt plus the deliverable checklist; then run the scoping gate. action:"list" filters by kind (task/method); action:"get" returns one template with its placeholders.

template.description: Template id, e.g. lit-review, ml-pipeline, replicate, ablation, review.

topic.description: Fills {topic} in the template (subject of the study).

domain.description: Optional domain override: finance, ai, medicine, industrial, or general.

schemas.name: rsx_source
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — sources. Record a paper/preprint/dataset/registry/report/news item with title, year, kind, reliability (primary/secondary/tertiary), DOI/authors/journal, and captured content (text or a file path). Captured content is stored as a content-addressed artifact and hashed; the survey gate needs 8 sources, 2 primary, 1 from 2023+, captured content, a disconfirming search, a coverage map, two independent primary sources and a risk-of-bias assessment on every primary source. Record lineage (derivedFrom/relation) so eight copies of one press release are not counted as eight independent confirmations; riskOfBias high/some-concerns needs robNote. action:"update" patches independence/design/riskOfBias/robNote/lineage/capture fields. action:"import" accepts BibTeX, CSL-JSON (Zotero) or RIS, detects the format when format:"auto", deduplicates DOI/title, and imports up to 100 records. action:"bibtex" renders references.bib; action:"export" returns BibTeX, CSL-JSON or RIS for the whole ledger; action:"lookup" resolves one DOI through Crossref and returns a sourceDraft ready for action:"add". action:"screen" records one candidate decision at stage title/abstract/full-text with an optional exclusion reason; action:"prisma" returns the candidate decisions and PRISMA 2020 flow counts. action:"list" returns rows; ids look like S-0001 and are cited in manuscripts as [[src:S-0001]].

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

candidate.description: Screening candidate id, e.g. R-0001 (screen). Omit to create or reuse one by DOI/title.

source.description: Optional S-0001 to link a candidate to a ledger source and copy missing bibliographic fields.

stage.description: Screening stage: title, abstract, or full-text.

decision.description: include, exclude, or maybe at the selected stage.

reason.description: Exclusion reason code; required when decision is exclude.

duplicateOf.description: Retained candidate id when this record is a duplicate; omit stage/decision.

reviewer.description: Reviewer name recorded with the decision (default agent).

doi.description: DOI (without https://doi.org/). Used by add and lookup.

authors.description: Author list, "A and B" or a plain string.

bibtex.description: BibTeX text: one record for add, many for import (legacy alias for data).

data.description: Reference-manager export text for import: BibTeX, CSL-JSON or RIS.

format.description: Import/export format; defaults to auto for import and bibtex for export.

reliability.description: Primary = original data/paper; secondary = review/news; tertiary = index.

content.description: Captured full text / abstract / key passages (stored as an artifact).

path.description: Absolute path to a captured text/PDF-extract file (alternative to content).

retracted.description: Mark a source as retracted; citing it blocks the audit.

independence.description: Independence of a primary source from the other cited evidence.

design.description: Study design (RCT, cohort, DOE, in-vitro, benchmark, …).

riskOfBias.description: Risk-of-bias judgement for a primary source.

robNote.description: Concrete reason and expected direction of bias when riskOfBias is not low.

derivedFrom.description: Source id this item derives from (lineage).

relation.description: Lineage relation when derivedFrom is set.

lineageNote.description: How the derivation works (shared cohort, reused dataset, …).

captureMethod.description: How full text was captured (html, pdf, api, manual).

capturedAt.description: Capture timestamp; defaults to now when content is supplied.

schemas.name: rsx_claim
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — claims and hypotheses. A hypothesis must state falsifier, killCriterion, predicted observation, metricName, metricUnit and a warrant (the rule that lets evidence support it); the hypothesis gate needs two supporting evidence rows, a counter-evidence search and a novelty check. action:"status" sets proposed/supported/contested/refuted with a reason; every claim must leave "proposed" before analyze/review gates pass. action:"update" records warrant/counterEvidence/certainty after creation. action:"sensitivity" records one robustness check (name, method, specification, result, direction, optional trace); schema-3 campaigns need at least one before the analyze gate passes. Use kind:"hypothesis" for the main testable claim (one per campaign is enough), kind:"claim" for supporting assertions.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

statement.description: The claim, stated so it could be false.

killCriterion.description: When to abandon the line of work.

warrant.description: The inferential rule that licenses evidence → claim (Toulmin warrant).

counterEvidence.description: What counter-evidence search was run and what it found, including a null result.

certainty.description: GRADE-style certainty of the evidence body (not the hypothesis).

reason.description: Why the status changed / why a protocol was amended.

method.description: Sensitivity method, e.g. leave-one-out, alternative-model, subgroup (sensitivity action).

specification.description: What exactly changed in this robustness check (sensitivity action).

result.description: Result under the alternative specification (sensitivity action).

direction.description: What happened to the conclusion (sensitivity action).

trace.description: Optional trace for the sensitivity result: run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#metric or source:S-0001.

notes.description: Caveats or interpretation for the sensitivity check.

schemas.name: rsx_evidence
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — link a claim to a source (S-0001), a run (R-xxxxxxxxxx) or a registered artifact (sha256:…), with relation supports/refutes/context plus an optional locator and quote. Evidence is the only way a claim becomes supported: the hypothesis gate requires two supporting rows, and the report lists every claim with its evidence count. action:"list" shows the ledger with the exact quote that backs each row.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

quote.description: The exact passage or metric that backs the claim.

schemas.name: rsx_run
schemas.description: Record a real execution (default: record only, the plugin does not run commands). Pass the exact command, status, seed, exit code, control:"negative" for the negative control, metrics as a JSON object, and optionally stdoutPath. Use action:"attach" with id + stdoutPath to fill a missing stdout artifact on an existing run; replay the exact command and verify the metrics match before attaching. The execute gate requires one successful seeded run with metrics, its exact command, and a really-run negative control. Metrics keys become traceable number sources: run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#key. Never invent a run: run the command yourself with the shell tool, then record it here with the real outputs.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

command.description: The exact command that was run.

control.description: Set "negative" for the negative control run.

stdoutPath.description: Absolute path to captured stdout/stderr (stored as an artifact).

id.description: Run id for get or attach.

schemas.name: rsx_number
schemas.description: Evidence ledger — numbers. Register every number that will appear in the manuscript with a trace: run:R-xxxxxxxxxx#metric for your own runs, source:S-0001 for literature values. The tool verifies the value against the traced run metric on write, returns the markdown token {{N-0001}}, and the analyze gate requires all traces to resolve and at least one uncertainty. Write numbers in the manuscript as {{N-0001}} — never type them by hand; the write gate flags orphan digits.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

uncertainty.description: CI / SD / SE / range, e.g. "95% CI 0.31–0.57".

schemas.name: rsx_extract
schemas.description: Evidence extraction matrix (Elicit-style): one row per source × dimension, with value, exact quote, locator and confidence. The matrix is exported as MATRIX.md/matrix.csv and shown in the panel. Use it for literature reviews and cross-paper comparison: dimensions are the columns, each source gets a row. The audit checks that a quote actually occurs in the captured source text. action:"matrix" returns the pivot table plus Markdown and CSV; action:"list" filters by source/dimension.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

dimension.description: Column name, e.g. sample_size / method / effect_size.

quote.description: Exact passage from the captured source supporting the value.

schemas.name: rsx_review
schemas.description: Automated reviewer (Claude Science-style): checks every manuscript citation resolves to a captured source, every quote occurs in the captured text, every number matches the run that produced it, every figure has figure+code+data provenance, the pre-registration still describes the executed analysis, and the negative control is real. Findings have severity blocking/major/minor/info. Only blocking findings stop the rsx_gate review gate; majors are for the human reviewer to resolve. The audit records a subject hash and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the decision, so any later edit makes it stale or invalid and the review gate asks for a fresh audit. action:"audit" runs and records the signed audit; action:"view" returns the latest audit + matrix; action:"list" shows audit history, signature status and freshness. For a domain campaign record the role reviews before auditing, otherwise the audit sees missing roles and blocks the review gate. action:"packet" builds a reviewer packet (claims with warrants/certainty, source independence, numbers, runs, ten review questions); action:"entailment" runs the lexical claim↔quote screen only. The screen checks that claim terms occur in the supporting quote — it is not semantic entailment, and a human still decides meaning.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

record.description: Set false to run a dry audit without appending to the ledger (default true).

schemas.name: rsx_artifact
schemas.description: Content-addressed artifacts: register a dataset, code file, environment lock, supplementary file or any other evidence with a role and a description. Bytes are hashed; the same content is never stored twice. Every artifact is exported under artifacts/ and appears in provenance.json and ro-crate-metadata.json. Use action:"list"/"get" to inspect roles, sizes and a short text preview. Figures should go through rsx_figure so figure+code+data are linked as one provenance unit.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

description.description: What this artifact is and how it was produced.

schemas.name: rsx_figure
schemas.description: Attach a figure with full provenance: the figure file, the exact code that drew it, the data it read, optionally the environment artifact, the run id, a plain-language description and a caption. The write gate blocks figures without figure+code+data. The audit also checks that every referenced artifact exists and that the run resolves; prose-only figures are not release quality. Paths are registered automatically; existing sha256: ids are accepted too.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

artifact.description: Figure image artifact id or path.

envArtifact.description: Environment lock artifact id or path.

description.description: Plain-language description of what the figure shows.

env.description: Environment note (versions / hardware) if not using envArtifact.

run.description: Run id that produced the figure.

source.description: Source id (e.g. S-0001) the figure is based on.

schemas.name: rsx_domain
schemas.description: Domain research profiles: finance, AI/ML, medicine/clinical and industrial/engineering. Each profile maps required protocol fields to pipeline stages and adds blocking domain checks (PRISMA ordering, OOS dates, review roles, monitoring, etc.); conditional fields switch off when the study design/risk tier makes them inapplicable. action:"list" returns the four profiles; action:"get" returns the selected profile, values, completeness and current gate; action:"set" selects a profile and optionally merges values; action:"check" evaluates one stage. Selecting a domain is not a compliance claim: the profile is a structured alignment checklist. Use rsx_campaign action:"monitor" for metrics/observations and action:"evaluate" for the 13-dimension loop score.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

domain.description: Profile id: finance, ai, medicine, industrial, or general (clear).

values.description: Field values keyed by profile field id; unknown ids are rejected. Text fields can be updated incrementally.

schemas.name: rsx_gate
schemas.description: The nine gates. action:"check" runs the gate for a stage (default: current) and records the result; action:"advance" advances only when the current stage passes, otherwise returns the blocking checks; action:"back" returns to an earlier stage with a reason. action:"review" records a structured review (reviewer, affiliation, conflict, independent, qualification, adversarial, verdict accept/minor/major/reject, issues with severity blocking/major/minor); the review gate needs two reviews and at least one adversarial. Review roles: a domain campaign needs one review per profile role (quant/risk, ml/safety, clinical/statistics, engineering/quality); pass role with the review. 0.5 reviews also declare affiliation, conflict and independent so role coverage is not a string match. Run check before advance so you can see the exact blocking codes. Gate results are append-only history. The review gate also requires a fresh, passing automated audit whose HMAC signature verifies (`rsx_review action:"audit"`); release requires `stateOk !== false`. action:"approve" records a named human approval bound to the current audit subject hash (it goes stale when substantive evidence changes); action:"waive" records an expiring, attributed waiver for one failing check; action:"waivers"/"approvals" list them. Waivers cannot cover integrity, audit signature, review independence, declaration, upstream-gate or human-approval checks.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

stage.description: Stage to check, or the target stage for back.

affiliation.description: Reviewer affiliation or independent capacity (review action). Required for new domain role reviews.

conflict.description: Conflict-of-interest declaration, e.g. "none" or a concrete competing interest (review action). Required for new domain role reviews.

independent.description: False when the reviewer is not independent of the work; role coverage requires true (default true).

role.description: Domain review role id (quant/risk, ml/safety, clinical/statistics, engineering/quality). Each domain role needs its own review.

approver.description: Human approver name (approve action); must not be the model name.

statement.description: What the approver is signing off on (at least 12 characters).

code.description: Gate check id to waive (waive action).

schemas.name: rsx_program
schemas.description: Research program orchestration above the nine gates. It records what a multi-agent or long-running research effort actually planned and decided, so the programme is auditable even when the agents are external. action:"plan" sets the objective and question list (each question needs an owner, priority and resolving source coverage); action:"perspective" records a stakeholder view and its sources; action:"autonomy" records maxCycles, stopCriteria, escalation and humanCheckpoints; action:"cycle" records one act→observe→decide step, refused once maxCycles is exhausted. action:"match" records a pairwise judgement between two claims (Elo bookkeeping, not truth); action:"rank" returns the current ranking; action:"quality" records the six-dimension rubric (factual accuracy, citation accuracy, completeness, source quality, tool efficiency, limitations); action:"contradiction" records conflicting evidence and its resolution. action:"list" returns the programme summary and completeness checks. Schema-4/5 campaigns must have a complete programme before the review gate passes: plan≥2 covered questions, perspectives≥2 with sources, autonomy policy, ≥1 cycle, ≥1 hypothesis/competing-claim match, a rubric row with overall≥0.7, and no open contradictions. The game is local and deterministic; it does not run agents or searches.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

question.description: A plan question to append, or the perspective question (plan/perspective).

coverage.description: Resolving source ids covering the plan question.

sources.description: Resolving source ids used by the perspective.

stopCriteria.description: When the autonomous loop stops (autonomy action).

escalation.description: When the loop escalates to a human (autonomy action).

humanCheckpoints.description: Where a human must confirm before continuing (autonomy action).

step.description: The action actually taken in this cycle (cycle action).

run.description: Optional R-xxxxxxxxxx run id linked to the cycle.

a.description: First claim id in a match (match action).

b.description: Second claim id in a match (match action).

criterion.description: The criterion used for the pairwise judgement (match action).

scores.description: Quality scores 0–1 for factual_accuracy, citation_accuracy, completeness, source_quality, tool_efficiency, limitations.

scope.description: What the quality rubric covered (quality action).

claim.description: Claim id for a contradiction (contradiction action).

evidenceA.description: First conflicting evidence ref: E-xxxx / S-xxxx / R-xxxxxxxxxx / sha256:….

resolution.description: How a resolved/explained contradiction was handled (at least 12 characters).

schemas.name: rsx_write
schemas.description: Writing and delivery. action:"manuscript" stores the draft (text or path) and runs the write gate; "declaration" records AI assistance + watermark + model + human reviewer + an AI/human contribution matrix; "render" writes REPORT.md, campaign.json, ledger.jsonl, declaration.md, STEWARDSHIP.md, references.bib, MATRIX.md, matrix.csv, AUDIT.md, REVIEW_PACKET.md, REPRO.md, repro.json, checksums.txt, AI_CONTRIBUTION.md, DOMAIN.md (when a domain profile is set), LOOP.md (when evaluated), provenance.json and ro-crate-metadata.json into the campaign exports folder. action:"export" additionally writes MANIFEST.json (per-file bytes + SHA-256 and the release gate), copies artifacts and builds BUNDLE.zip; the manifest does not hash itself or the archive. action:"repro" returns the executable reproduction manifest; action:"packet" returns the review packet; action:"report" returns the Markdown without writing. Manuscript rules: numbers as {{N-0001}}, sources as [[src:S-0001]]; the write gate rejects orphan digits and unknown refs.

campaign.description: Campaign id. Omit to use the current campaign.

model.description: Model / tool name for the declaration.

contributions.description: AI/human contribution matrix: [{actor:"ai"|"human", role, name, scope}]. Defaults to one AI drafting role plus the human reviewer.
